documents: Novak, Vrabec, Popit, Vizintin & Smuc (2023) Facies analysis, depositional activity, and internal structure of sieve deposits on an active alluvial fan. Earth Surface Processes and Landforms 48(3), 647-664 (published PDF)

entry.evidence: Our objective was to answer, at least in part, the open questions listed in the previous sections

steps.action: The authors take from the literature two rival accounts of open-framework fan deposits: Hooke's sieve deposition and Blair & McPherson's winnowing of matrix-rich debris flows.
steps.quote: However, the sieve-lobe paradigm was subsequently opposed by several studies

steps.action: They state three open questions: no quantitative facies analysis, no long-term monitoring linked to rainfall triggers, and no subsurface imaging of a sieve-lobe fan.
steps.quote: the subsurface geometry of such a fan has not yet been documented

steps.action: They pose rivals for formation frequency: rare deposition driven by extreme rainfall versus frequent deposition under regular meteorological conditions.
steps.quote: whether the sieve-lobe formation is an infrequent deposition event driven by extreme and infrequent precipitation

steps.action: They select the active, fines-poor Suhi vrh fan, which has a nearby meteorological station, as a site where sieve deposition happens live.
steps.quote: makes this study site an ideal location for studying active sieve-lobe deposition

steps.action: They catalogue lobe structures, assign relative ages from lichen coating, and sample 11 unreworked lobes and sublobes at proximal, middle and distal positions (618 kg).
steps.quote: Eleven individual sieve lobes and sublobes evenly distributed on the active surface of the alluvial fan were distinguished and sampled

steps.action: They dry-sieve the samples, measure manually the clasts over 64 mm, run laser granulometry in triplicate on fines, and classify shape and roundness visually.
steps.quote: Each sample was measured three times and an average was calculated from the three measurements.

steps.action: They set up repeat UAV structure-from-motion surveys (10 surveys, 2019-2021) with a permanent network of 17 GCPs and produce 5 cm DEMs and 1 cm orthomosaics.
steps.quote: Point clouds and derived DEMs and orthorectified photomosaics were produced by structure-from-motion photogrammetric reconstruction using Agisoft Metashape software.

steps.action: They check the survey premise by repeating the GNSS surveys of the GCPs and by comparing RTK/PPK georeferencing with the other UAVs.
steps.quote: no significant difference in survey precision was observed compared to other UAVs used in the study

steps.action: They compute DEMs of difference and cut/fill volumes, masked to unvegetated active areas, and class changes as substantial, moderate or minor.
steps.quote: the DoDs and volumetric calculations were limited to manually created polygonal areas covering only those areas of active sediment transport

steps.action: Following earlier studies, they fix a trigger threshold of 50 mm per 24 h (with 48 h events and snow as secondary factors) for pairing changes with rainfall.
steps.quote: the threshold for a potentially triggering precipitation event was set at 50 mm of rainfall in 24 h

steps.action: They acquire three 50 MHz GPR profiles, one longitudinal and two transverse, across the active fan and process them with topographic correction.
steps.quote: the 50 MHz antenna offers the best compromise between penetration depth and resolution of subsurface structures

steps.action: They describe the lobe morphology: lobate fronts, sigmoidal longitudinal and hummocky transverse profiles, non-erosional stacked contacts, undamaged vegetation, and crude stratification.
steps.quote: Stacked and intertwined lobes form a sieve-lobe complex in which there are no erosional contacts between lobes

steps.action: They establish that downward coarsening, unimodality and less than 2.5% mud repeat across old, young and sublobes, and quantify the differences by age.
steps.quote: Granulometric analysis shows a general tendency of increase in mean clast size from the proximal to the distal parts of each sieve lobe

steps.action: They pair each of the 9 survey intervals with the strongest 24 h or 48 h rainfall event and its magnitude of surface change (Table 2).
steps.quote: Changes occurred after intense 24 or 48 h rainfall events.

steps.action: They quantify the net deposition per event, up to 1279.5 m3 for the 2/8/2021 event.
steps.quote: with the largest increase of 1279.5 m3 on 2/8/2021

steps.action: When the 12/10/2020 event exceeded the threshold but produced no change, they invoke a rain-to-snow transition rather than revising the threshold.
steps.quote: Precipitation on 12/10/2020 exceeded the 50 mm threshold (57.4 mm). However, this precipitation event transitioned from rain to snowfall

steps.action: They describe the radargrams: progradational sigmoid reflectors in GPR-1, hummocky discontinuous reflectors in GPR-2 and GPR-3, and signal loss at about 15 m.
steps.quote: The reflectors are progradational and exhibit sigmoid shapes

steps.action: They reject the suggestion of Nemec & Postma (1993) that lobe sediment is bimodal, because all samples but one are unimodal.
steps.quote: This idea is not supported by our results, because granulometry clearly shows that all samples except one are unimodal

steps.action: They distinguish sieve lobes from grain-flow deposits, which have a similar proximal-distal grading, by the slope angle at which they form.
steps.quote: compared to sieve lobes, grain flows occur on considerably steeper surfaces

steps.action: They attribute the exceptions to the grading trend in SO 1 and SO 2 to sampling across poorly defined contacts between lobes.
steps.quote: discrepancy in percentages can be attributed to the sampling strategy

steps.action: They argue that the increase in fines with lobe age (weathering, secondary deposition) does not fit Blair & McPherson's winnowing mechanism.
steps.quote: Measurements of the higher proportion of small-grained particles in older sieve lobes do not confirm the mechanism of winnowing of primary matrix-rich debris flows

steps.action: They compare the crude stratification with Milana's growth scenarios and interpret each layer as a stacked sublobe.
steps.quote: Crude stratification of lobes could be the result of such growth, where each layer in a single lobe represents one sublobe

steps.action: They keep the claim that sieve lobes form several times a year under common rainfall events rather than extreme ones.
steps.quote: Our data clearly show that the rainfall events that triggered sieve-lobe deposition were not extreme meteorological events

steps.action: For the 4/11/2021 event (67.5 mm, only moderate change), they assume rainfall spread over the day, which allowed infiltration.
steps.quote: We assume that rainfall did not occur in a short period of a few hours but extended throughout the entire day.

steps.action: They weigh avulsion mechanisms (channel backfilling, channel plugging, reduced permeability) and favour backfilling on the DoD evidence.
steps.quote: Based on DoDs, we assume that in our case avulsion occurred due to channel backfilling.

steps.action: They match the erosion-above-deposition DoD patterns to the model of Nemec & Postma, in which infiltrated water emerges downslope.
steps.quote: The findings of this study, based on surface monitoring, corroborate field-based studies of previous works

steps.action: They interpret the GPR reflectors, which resemble the surface lobe cross-sections, as stacked sieve lobes in the upper 10-15 m.
steps.quote: confirm previous estimates that entire fans may be predominantly or entirely built of sieve lobes

steps.action: They conclude that the fan is built predominantly of sieve lobes, supporting Milana's paradigm.
steps.quote: The GPR data indicate that the upper 10 to 15 m of the studied alluvial fan consist predominantly of stacked sieve lobes

tree.answer: Sieve-lobe deposits on an active gravel-rich alpine fan
Deposits are observed directly; deposition is inferred from repeat UAV DEMs and the subsurface from GPR
Quantify the facies, link deposition to rainfall triggers, and image the subsurface
Sieve deposition vs winnowing of debris flows; frequent vs extreme-event formation
Partly: grain-size trends with age and rainfall frequency are argued to discriminate between the rivals
Found: natural rainfall events on a live fan

tree.question: 6b
tree.answer: Yes: 9 survey intervals and 11 lobes of different age and size
Partly: exceptions are explained by auxiliaries (snowfall, rainfall duration, sampling)
Kept: fan built mainly of sieve lobes, which form sub-annually after rainfall over 50-60 mm/24 h
Two anonymous reviewers are acknowledged; no review file was supplied

end.claim: The upper 10-15 m of the Suhi vrh fan consist predominantly of stacked sieve lobes, which form sub-annually after common rainfall events; this supports the concept that sieve lobes are main fan building blocks.

decisive_move.sentence: Interpreting the GPR reflectors as stacked sieve lobes, by their resemblance to the surface lobe geometry, gives the subsurface claim that no earlier study had.

gates.evidence: The open questions about the sieve-lobe paradigm directed the GPR and monitoring campaigns, but no hypothesis test was designed. The 50 mm/24 h threshold was taken from prior studies before pairing events with surface changes (p. 651). The threshold failed twice (12/10/2020, 4/11/2021) and was protected by auxiliaries. The GPR claim rests on resemblance to surface forms, with no core or exposure check.

imports.item: Structure-from-motion photogrammetry from UAV imagery (Agisoft Metashape)
Laser granulometer with dynamic image analysis (Fritsch Analysette 22-28)
Small unmanned aircraft (DJI Phantom 4 Pro, Mavic Mini, Phantom 4 RTK)

novelty_claims.quote: the internal geometry of sieve-lobe built alluvial fans has not yet been imaged by subsurface methods
the sieve-lobe facies has been defined largely based on qualitative field observations without quantitative sedimentological analyses
None of the studies observed active sieve-lobe deposition over an extended (i.e. annual) period

limits: Sub-claims sit at different statuses: the rainfall-trigger relation (sub-annual formation after events over 50-60 mm/24 h) is regularity_in_range for one fan and three years; the event volumes (up to 1279.5 m3) are estimate_with_resolution, but no uncertainty or level of detection is reported for the DoDs, although Wheaton et al. (2010) is cited (inference: no threshold applied); the facies description is regularity_in_range across 11 lobes. Relative lobe ages come from visual lichen coating. Trigger events are attributed by timing ('most likely'). Anomalous events are explained post hoc by snowfall or rainfall duration rather than tested. The GPR interpretation has no ground truth and does not reach the fan base. A single fan is studied, with no comparison site. The winnowing rival is dismissed by argument, not by a discriminating test. No review file was supplied, so the review history is unknown, although two reviewers are thanked. Data are available only on request. The trace_series composition is a judgment: the walk mixes live-event monitoring (natures_repetition) with trace interpretation (GPR).

disagreements.target: Blair & McPherson (1992, 1994, 1995, 2009): open-framework lobes as winnowed debris flows
disagreements.support: Fines increase with lobe age, which they attribute to weathering and secondary deposition and argue does not fit winnowing.
disagreements.quote: do not confirm the mechanism of winnowing of primary matrix-rich debris flows [...] )

disagreements.target: Nemec & Postma (1993): sieve-lobe sediment can be bimodal
disagreements.support: Granulometry shows that all samples except one are unimodal.
disagreements.quote: This idea is not supported by our results, because granulometry clearly shows that all samples except one are unimodal

disagreements.target: Nemec & Postma (1993): sieve lobes are a minor part of fan composition
disagreements.support: GPR profiles at Suhi vrh show the upper 10-15 m dominated by stacked sieve lobes.
disagreements.quote: in the findings of Nemec and Postma (1993) sieve lobes account for only a minor percentage of alluvial fan composition

disagreements.target: View linking sieve-lobe deposition to high-intensity, low-frequency precipitation (Morgan & Craddock, 2017)
disagreements.support: The triggering events at Suhi vrh were common events that occur six to eight times a year.
disagreements.quote: the rainfall events that triggered sieve-lobe deposition were not extreme meteorological events but are very common annual precipitation events

alternatives_considered.reason: Best compromise between penetration depth and resolution in carbonate gravels (Sass & Krautblatter, 2007)

alternatives_considered.chosen: DoDs limited to manually delineated unvegetated active areas
alternatives_considered.alternatives: DoDs over the full DEM including the vegetated inactive area
alternatives_considered.reason: Vegetation would introduce inaccuracies (cf. Westoby et al., 2012)

alternatives_considered.chosen: GCP-based georeferencing, with RTK/PPK on some surveys
Trigger threshold of 50 mm in 24 h
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Intense 48 h rainfall events; snowfall and snow cover as modifiers
alternatives_considered.reason: Following Guzzetti et al. (2007), ARSO (2009, 2021b) and Novak et al. (2020)

alternatives_considered.alternatives: Channel plugging by sediment of earlier events; reduced permeability from finer deposition (Milana, 2010)

alternatives_considered.chosen: Physical weathering and secondary sedimentation for higher fines in older lobes
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Aeolian dust or pedogenesis; winnowing of matrix-rich debris flows
alternatives_considered.reason: Highly fractured Conzen dolomite; fines increase with age
